title: DXF owner graph versus physical OBJECTS record order
mode: Primary-source DXF reference and open-source implementation review
scope: Audit the PAR-20/7G.3 owner/order test lane against Autodesk DXF references.
Compare graph ownership and exporter ordering models in ezdxf and LibreDWG.
Refine minimum-fast-slice and optional peer-check criteria without broadening support claims.

sources.revision: Public Autodesk Help pages reviewed 2026-10-20; page revisions are as exposed by the URLs.
sources.observed: The OBJECTS section example begins with the named-object root DICTIONARY; common object and per-object tables define owner pointers and specific dictionary ownership. The pages do not establish a universal owner-record-before-child-record rule for all OBJECTS records.
sources.limits: The sample is an example, not proof that no specific object/version has additional ordering requirements. Per-object owner definitions remain authoritative for those object types.

sources.project: ezdxf DXF object graph and exporter
sources.observed: The source documents owner linking, root owner zero/orphan handling, one-parent ownership, owner-path reconstruction, and ordered tags within an object's own export.
sources.limits: This is one peer implementation, not normative DXF text; reviewed sources do not claim a universal cross-record owner preorder. The pass did not build or run ezdxf.

sources.revision: Public manual and moving master source reviewed 2026-10-20.
sources.observed: The tool has explicit ASCII and binary DXF output routes, while the manual categorizes some object/class states as unstable or unhandled rather than conflating writer availability with complete object support.
sources.limits: No pinned LibreDWG build was selected or run; a successful conversion cannot establish libdxfrw behavior or complete typed semantics.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-20/7G.3: use unique handles, exact dictionary key-to-child identity, exact owner-to-parent identity, reciprocal references where defined, and strict readback as core graph assertions.
PAR-20/7G.3: reserve broad physical owner-before-child ordering for documented writer contracts or pinned consumer/version regressions; distinguish it from normative DXF conformance.
PAR-20/7G.3: retain existing order assertions as local serializer regressions unless a specific assertion is shown to encode an unsupported rule or unnecessary cost.
PAR-07/S8: interpret peer conversion and reopen outcomes with object diagnostics and route boundaries, not process exit alone.
Validation cadence: changed target, direct selector, and owning fast CTest per slice; peer and native consumer checks only at composed milestones.

planChanges: Recorded that Autodesk's OBJECTS example makes root-first a separately meaningful shape but does not establish a universal cross-record owner-before-child rule.
Promoted exact owner/key/handle graph closure and strict readback as the minimum PAR-20/7G.3 semantic test; scoped physical order to explicit writer contracts or pinned consumer regressions.
Kept existing passing physical-order checks classified as deterministic local serializer regressions rather than deleting them based on absence of a universal rule.
Kept peer conversion/reopen and full-suite work outside per-slice fast validation; no local code or test changes were made.
limitations: The review is a focused reference and source review, not a complete per-object audit of every DXF version.
No peer source checkout or executable was built or run, and no CAD consumer or external drawing was used.
An object/version-specific ordering constraint may exist outside the reviewed examples and must be checked against its own authoritative reference or a pinned regression.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain external-only, advisory, and non-promoting.
